g.title: n1240
g.text: Terminate SSL on the load balancer

g.title: n1241
g.text: Pre-warm your ELBs if you're expecting heavy traffic

g.title: n1243
g.text: Use termination protection for non-auto-scaling instances

g.title: n1245
g.text: Use reserved instances to save big $$$

g.title: n1252
g.text: Prefer EC2 roles over app level IAM account

g.title: n1253
g.text: Assign permissions to groups, not users

g.title: n1255
g.text: Use CloudTrail to keep an audit log

g.title: n1257
g.text: Use "-" instead of "." in bucket names for SSL

g.title: n1259
g.text: Having CloudFront in front of S3 is optional (but it can help)

g.title: n1260
g.text: Use random strings at the start of your keys

g.title: n1262
g.text: Do not store application state on servers

g.title: n1263
g.text: Store extra information in your logs

g.title: n1264
g.text: If you need to interact with AWS, use the official SDK

g.title: n1265
g.text: Have tools to view application logs

g.title: n1267
g.text: Use multiple API keys for different purposes

g.title: n1268
g.text: Use multi-factor auth for IAM users

g.title: n1270
g.text: Specify a directory on S3 for Hive results

g.title: n1271
g.text: Use configuration endpoints over individual endpoints

g.title: n1272
g.text: Scale down on INSUFFICIENT_DATA as well as ALARM

g.title: n1273
g.text: Use ELB health check instead of EC2 health checks

g.title: n1274
g.text: Only use the availability zones (AZs) your ELB is configured for

g.title: n1275
g.text: Avoid multiple scaling triggers on the same group

g.title: n1276
g.text: Disable SSH access to all servers (Optional)

g.title: n1277
g.text: Care about services as a whole instead of servers

g.title: n1280
g.text: Everyone gets an IAM account. Never login to the master

g.title: n1281
g.text: Get your alerts to become notifications

g.title: n1283
g.text: Your application may require changes to work on AWS

g.title: n1284
g.text: Always be redundant across availability zones (AZs)

g.title: n1285
g.text: Be aware of AWS service limits before you deploy

g.title: n1286
g.text: Decide on a naming convention early, and stick to it

g.title: n1287
g.text: Decide on a key-management strategy from the start

g.title: n1288
g.text: Make sure AWS is right for your workload

g.title: n1289
g.text: Set up event subscriptions for failover

g.title: n1304
g.text: Concatenate CSS into a single file

g.title: n1307
g.text: Use preconnect to load your fonts faster

g.title: n1308
g.text: Keep the web font size under 300kb

g.title: n1310
g.text: Keep an eye on the size of dependencies

g.title: n1311
g.text: Minified HTML - Remove comments and whitespaces

g.title: n1313
g.text: Prefer using vector image rather than bitmap images

g.title: n1314
g.text: Set width and height attributes on images (aspect ratio)

g.title: n1317
g.text: Ensure to serve images that are close to your display size

g.title: n1319
g.text: Keep your dependencies up to date

g.title: n1320
g.text: Check for performance problems in your JavaScript files

g.title: n1321
g.text: Service Workers for caching / performing heavy tasks

g.title: n1322
g.text: Cookie size should be less than 4096 bytes

g.title: n1323
g.text: Keep the cookie count less than 20

g.title: n1324
g.text: Keep your page weight < 1500 KB (ideally < 500 kb)

g.title: n1325
g.text: Keep your page load time < 3 seconds

g.title: n1328
g.text: Compress your images / keep the image count low

g.title: n1330
g.text: Keep the Time To First Byte < 1.3 seconds

g.title: n1331
g.text: Non Blocking JavaScript: Use async / defer

g.title: n1333
g.text: Minified CSS - Remove comments, whitespaces etc

g.title: n1334
g.text: Inline the Critical CSS (above the fold CSS)

g.text: Serve files from the same protocol

g.title: n1349
g.text: Audit your design and implementation with unit/integration tests

g.title: n1350
g.text: Use a code review process and disregard self-approval

g.title: n1351
g.text: Continuously run security analysis on your code

g.title: n1352
g.text: Check your dependencies for known vulnerabilities

g.title: n1353
g.text: Design a rollback solution for deployments

g.title: n1359
g.text: Avoid returning sensitive data (credentials, tokens, etc)

g.title: n1360
g.text: Return proper response codes as per the operation

g.title: n1361
g.text: Use centralized logins for all services and components

g.title: n1362
g.text: Use agents to monitor all requests, responses, and errors

g.title: n1363
g.text: Use alerts for SMS, Slack, Email, Kibana, CloudWatch, etc

g.title: n1364
g.text: Ensure you aren’t logging any sensitive data

g.title: n1365
g.text: Use an IDS and/or IPS system to monitor everything

g.title: n1366
g.text: Limit requests (throttling) to avoid DDoS / brute force

g.title: n1367
g.text: Use HTTPS on server side and secure ciphers

g.title: n1368
g.text: Use HSTS header with SSL to avoid SSL strip attacks

g.title: n1370
g.text: Private APIs should only be accessible from safe-listed IPs

g.title: n1371
g.text: Use good JWT Secret to make brute-force attacks difficult

g.title: n1372
g.text: Do not extract the algorithm from the header, use backend

g.title: n1373
g.text: Make token expiration (TTL, RTTL) as short as possible

g.title: n1374
g.text: Avoid storing sensitive data in JWT payload

g.title: n1375
g.text: Keep the payload small to reduce the size of the JWT

g.title: n1377
g.text: Avoid response_type=token and try to exchange for code

g.title: n1378
g.text: Use state parameter to prevent CSRF attacks

g.title: n1379
g.text: Have default scope, and validate scope for each application

g.title: n1380
g.text: Check if all endpoints are protected behind authentication to avoid broken authentication process

g.title: n1381
g.text: Avoid user’s personal ID in resource URLs (e.g., users/242/orders)

g.title: n1382
g.text: Prefer using UUID over auto-increment IDs

g.title: n1383
g.text: Disable entity parsing if parsing XML to avoid XXE attacks

g.title: n1384
g.text: Disable entity expansion if using XML, YAML, or similar

g.title: n1385
g.text: Use a CDN for file uploads

g.title: n1386
g.text: Avoid HTTP blocking when handling large amounts of data

g.title: n1387
g.text: Make sure debug mode is off in production

g.title: n1389
g.text: Limit requests (throttling) to avoid DDoS / brute force

g.title: n1390
g.text: Use HTTPS on server side and secure ciphers

g.title: n1391
g.text: Use HSTS header with SSL to avoid SSL strip attacks

g.title: n1393
g.text: Private APIs should only be accessible from safe-listed IPs

g.title: n1395
g.text: Do not reinvent the wheel in authentication mechanisms

g.title: n1396
g.text: Use ‘Max Retry’ and jail features in login

g.title: n1397
g.text: Use encryption on all sensitive data

g.title: n1404
g.text: Use connection pooling to reduce connection overhead

g.title: n1405
g.text: Fine-tune connection pool settings (e.g., max connections, idle timeout, connection reuse params) to optimize resource utilization and prevent connection exhaustion

g.title: n1407
g.text: Keep an eye on and fine-tune ORM queries

g.title: n1408
g.text: Utilize lazy loading, eager loading, and batch processing to optimize data retrieval

g.title: n1409
g.text: Implement efficient pagination for large datasets

g.title: n1410
g.text: Avoid SELECT * queries and fetch only required columns

g.title: n1411
g.text: Consider denormalizing schema for read-heavy workloads and reducing JOIN operations

g.title: n1412
g.text: Optimize JOIN operations and avoid unnecessary joins

g.title: n1413
g.text: Regularly clean up unused data and perform maintenance tasks like vacuuming, indexing, and optimizing queries

g.title: n1414
g.text: Enable slow-query logging and monitor it

g.title: n1415
g.text: Set up database replication for redundancy and improved read performance

g.title: n1416
g.text: Use DB sharding for data distribution if required

g.title: n1417
g.text: Use profiling tools offered by your database

g.title: n1420
g.text: Implement efficient pagination for large datasets

g.title: n1421
g.text: Minimise unnecessary processing or expensive computation on the server.

g.title: n1422
g.text: Conduct regular performance testing and benchmarking to identify performance regressions, track improvements, and fine-tune optimization efforts over time

g.title: n1423
g.text: Use Horizontal or Vertical scaling whatever appropriate

g.title: n1424
g.text: Use load balancing to distribute traffic across servers

g.title: n1425
g.text: Offload heavy tasks to background jobs or queues

g.title: n1426
g.text: Utilize message brokers for asynchrnous communication between services.

g.title: n1427
g.text: Implement comprehensive monitoring and logging to track performance metrics and troubleshoot issues

g.title: n1428
g.text: Use tools like Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack.

g.title: n1429
g.text: Use asynchronous logging mechanisms to minimise the logging overhead.

g.title: n1431
g.text: Use cache-aside, write-through, or read-through caching patterns based on your application requirements

g.title: n1432
g.text: Use proper cache-invalidation strategies to ensure data consistency and prevent stale content

g.title: n1434
g.text: Profile your code to identify performance bottlenecks

g.title: n1435
g.text: Optimize algorithms and data structures used

g.title: n1436
g.text: Identify and optimize critical paths or frequently accessed endpoints for overall system health.

g.title: n1437
g.text: Consider using compiled languages like Go or Rust for performance-critical parts of your backend.

g.title: n1438
g.text: Look into different architectural styles (SOA, Micro services) and decompose services if required.

g.title: n1439
g.text: Set appropriate connection timeouts and implement efficient retry mechanism to handle network issues

g.title: n1440
g.text: Batch similar requests together to minimize overhead and reduce the number of round trips.

g.title: n1441
g.text: Minimize network latency by hosting your backend close to your users

g.title: n1442
g.text: Utilize HTTP keep-alive to reduce connection overhead

g.title: n1443
g.text: Use CDNs for static and frequently accessed assets

g.title: n1444
g.text: Prefetch or preload resources, data, or dependencies needed for subsequent requests to minimize latency

g.title: n1445
g.text: Keep your dependencies up to date

g.title: n1446
g.text: Implement proper authentication and authorization to prevent unauthorized access

g.title: n1447
g.text: Implement request throttling and rate limiting

g.title: n1448
g.text: Regularly audit and update security measures
